subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Hit the nail on the head

options.text: To be exactly right about something

solution:
The correct answer is **To be exactly right about something.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom **"Hit the nail on the head" **is** "To be exactly right about something ."**
 
• **Hit the nail on the head** refers to being completely accurate about something.
 
 
• **​Example:** *He hit the nail on the head when he told the qualities of the school.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **To be exactly right about something.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Let's look at the meaning and examples of some idioms of the play **"Hit."**

 
 

 **Idioms**
 **Meaning**
 **Example**
 
 

 **Hit the ground running**
 to begin something right immediately with tremendous enthusiasm, without more instruction, training, or support
 *I am ready to hit the ground in the morning. I am all prepared for the interview.*
 
 

 **Hit the dust**
 when a failure isn't extreme or catastrophic, but just that it didn't happen
 *I was working on this interview all night hoping to get the job but in the end, it just hit the dust.*
